mindSpirit.heading: 4. Emotions, Mind, Spirit and Community
mindSpirit.subtitle: Reconnecting with ourselves and with our tribe.
mindSpirit.breakHeading: The Digital Revolution and Urbanisation (20th-21st century): Goodbye to the Tribe
mindSpirit.breakIntro: Before this, human beings never lived alone. «Loneliness» was a biological death sentence. Spirit and mind were fed by ritual, by the silence of nature and by the support of the group.
mindSpirit.changeText: We went from the «village», where everyone knew each other, to the anonymous big city, and finally to the digital hyper-link — social media that connects us with thousands while isolating us physically from everyone.
mindSpirit.impactText: Chronic loneliness appeared. The brain reads isolation as constant danger, and anxiety follows. We lost rites of passage and contact with the earth (natural spirituality), and replaced them with the mental «noise» of constant comparison and empty productivity.
mindSpirit.mismatchHeading: The «Evolutionary Mismatch» in Mind and Spirit
mindSpirit.mismatchIntro: Your brain still expects to look someone in the eye while you talk, to be recognised by your community for what you do, and to feel part of something bigger than yourself — nature, or purpose.
mindSpirit.offer2: Newscasts full of fear instead of stories around a fire.
mindSpirit.offer3: Fierce competition instead of tribal collaboration.
mindSpirit.callout: This pillar recognises that health is not only physical. It centres on emotional care, mental clarity and connection with others. «Spirit and community» health means feeling part of something bigger, keeping healthy relationships, and holding a clear purpose that drives the other three pillars.

movement.heading: 3. Movement and Exercise
movement.subtitle: Pushing back on a sedentary daily life.
movement.breakHeading: The Industrial Revolution (18th-19th century): Goodbye to Movement
movement.breakIntro: Before this, most of humanity worked the land, hunted or did manual work. Movement was not «exercise» — it was survival.
movement.changeText: The move from agrarian to industrial and then post-industrial societies took work out of open spaces and physical tasks and into indoor settings and mental tasks. A «chair and screen» job took hold: low physical demand and long days sitting down.
movement.impactText: Structural sedentarism appeared. For the first time in history, human beings began spending 8 or 12 hours sitting or standing in one place, under roofs that hid the sun from us — with machines replacing physical effort, opening the door to chronic sedentarism and many modern illnesses such as obesity and cardiovascular risk.
movement.callout: This pillar is about pushing back on a sedentary life by working physical activity into daily life. It is not limited to the gym: it covers walking, running, playing football or any form of functional movement. The aim is for people to find pleasure in physical effort and keep it up.

nutrition.heading: 2. Natural, Nourishing Food
nutrition.subtitle: Reconnecting with the source and with real food.
nutrition.breakHeading: The Green Revolution and Ultra-Processed Food (post-WWII)
nutrition.breakIntro: This is where eating broke. In the 1950s the priority was feeding a population that was exploding, and quantity won over quality.
nutrition.changeText: Refined vegetable oils appeared, along with white flour at scale and sugar in everything.
nutrition.impactText: We went from eating «food from the earth» to «edible products» designed in labs to be addictive but nutritionally empty.
nutrition.evidence: Since the post-war years, the drive to produce lots of cheap calories (the Green Revolution plus food industrialisation) eased the shift towards ultra-processed food built on sugar, flour and refined oils. It solved much of acute hunger, but at the cost of diets that are less diverse and more «laboratory-made» — today strongly tied to chronic disease and environmental damage. Going back to patterns built on minimally processed, varied, locally sourced food fits human and planetary health far better.
nutrition.callout: More than a diet, this pillar is about the connection to the source. It encourages real, local food, and builds the bridge between farmers and the people who eat.
nutrition.includes1: Backing restaurants that offer nourishing options.
nutrition.includes2: Encouraging people to grow their own (urban gardens or permaculture cells).
nutrition.includes3: Building a setting where choosing healthy food is the easiest option.

sleep.heading: 1. Sleep and Rest
sleep.subtitle: The ground floor of biological recovery and long-term health.
sleep.lightHeading: The Invention of Electric Light (1879): The End of Natural Sleep
sleep.lightIntro: This is perhaps the harshest turning point for our brain. Before Thomas Edison and artificial light, our circadian rhythm — the internal clock — was perfectly in step with the sun.
sleep.changeText: Night stopped being dark. We could work, eat and socialise long after sunset.
sleep.impactText: The body stopped producing melatonin properly. We began stealing hours from rest, which set off the chronic stress and inflammation we now see everywhere.
sleep.processesHeading: How many processes depend on sleep?
sleep.processesIntro: Sleep takes part in many essential functions, not just one:
sleep.brainText: memory and learning, synaptic plasticity, emotional and mood regulation.
sleep.metabolismText: regulating spend and replenishment of energy, anabolism, cell maintenance and clearing the brain's «waste» (the glymphatic system).
sleep.immuneText: defence against infection, response to vaccines, and control of the inflammation tied to cancer, depression and cardiovascular disease.
sleep.cardiovascularText: blood pressure, glucose, stress hormones, appetite hormones, reproductive health.
sleep.homeostasisText: balance across organ systems, metabolism, and psychological and social state.
sleep.evidence: The scientific evidence shows that sleep is involved in practically every critical process of body and mind. It is not a luxury: it is the physiological base of attention, memory, emotional stability, metabolism, immunity and long-term cardiovascular health.
sleep.callout: This pillar is the ground floor of biological recovery. It is not just about «sleeping», but about improving your sleep hygiene so body and mind can properly repair themselves. At {brand}, the aim is for technology to help track and encourage routines that respect circadian rhythms.

The messages you send to the chatbot.
Information you voluntarily share related to sleep, diet, exercise, or emotional well-being habits.
Basic technical data necessary for the operation of the service (such as date and time of interaction).
